| step | problem | world it is evaluated on |

### problem_chain

**Tree derived from the policy and the world alone.**

Root: the customer asks for **a service credit** → `cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement`
(`trigger: on_request`, subject `cafe_service_credit_issued`).

Reading that policy's rule, the one prerequisite sentence it carries is
> "The credit allowed is not worked out until a management fee invoiced for the billing period the
> claim concerns stands on the contract's ledger."

**Judged against the raw DB at `frozen_time`, this state already holds.** The computation counts the
service credit claims standing **approved** over the claim window; every one of them names, in
`cafe_service_requests.related_reference`, an invoice that already stands as a `management_fee` row on
`cafe_ledger`:

| approved claim (`created_at`) | `related_reference` | matching `cafe_ledger` row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-04-15 13:22 CDT | INV-CF-301447 | management_fee 2025-03-12, service_period 2025-03 |
| 2025-07-09 16:41 CDT | INV-CF-315209 | management_fee 2025-07-12, service_period 2025-07 |
| 2025-09-23 08:58 CDT | INV-CF-322310 | management_fee 2025-09-12, service_period 2025-09 |
| 2025-12-18 15:07 CST | INV-CF-333158 | management_fee 2025-12-12, service_period 2025-12 |
| 2026-01-27 09:36 CST | INV-CF-336702 | management_fee 2026-01-12, service_period 2026-01 |

The caller names the period herself — "the last stretch being in **January**" — and the January
management fee invoice (INV-CF-336702, posted 2026-01-12, `service_period` 2026-01) is on the ledger.
So the prerequisite the policy states is **satisfied at the opening**, and the sentence tells a
faithful reader nothing to do.

The tree the author evidently intends is
`service credit → management fee invoice → confirm service model change`, and the *second* edge is
genuinely unmet: `cafe_contracts.variant_name` = "Limited Service Cafe" while the approved request
`6cb121a5-5cd7-4bd3-8bcb-2fdfcca606f7` (created 2026-02-02, `request_status` approved) carries
`requested_variant_name` = "Full Service Cafe", so
`cafe_ext_management_fee_invoice`'s sentence — "The management fee for a billing period is not worked
out before the service model standing on the contract is the one named on the contract's approved
change of service model." — is false at the opening. But that edge is only reached **through** the
first, and the first does not bind.

**Nodes, edges, kinds, topological order** (as declared): 
`cafe_ext_model_change_confirmation` →(value_input, gate `base_fee_usd`)→
`cafe_ext_management_fee_invoice` →(value_input, gate `fee_base_usd`)→
`cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement`. n = 2 prerequisite problems, floor max(n−1,1) = 1 value_input
edge; both edges are `value_input`. No cycle.

**Per-edge load-bearing run** (recomputed by substituting the world, not by reading any GT field):

- *edge 2→1*: skip the model-change write and recompute the management fee on the opening world —
  `variant_name` stays "Limited Service Cafe", `months_since_model_change` = MONTHS(2025-06-18,
  2026-02-17) = 7 ≠ 0 so the transition mean does not apply and `base_fee_usd` = 4,275.00 instead of
  7,265.26. The scored figure changes. **The edge bears weight.**
- *edge 3→2*: skip the management fee write and recompute the credit — `mgmt_invoices_3m` = 2 (not 3),
  so `fee_base_usd` falls to `P('management_fee_monthly_usd')` and the credit changes from 1,511.64 to
  641.25. **The edge bears weight** — but see the verdict: an edge can carry a value and still not be a
  prerequisite, because the policy sentence that is supposed to announce it is already true.

**Parallel edges.** None; the tree is a chain, so no two orders are defensible.

**No-wait argument.** Each resolving action is a single synchronous tool call available at once:
`confirm_service_model_change_fa28a84a` (the customer's own, handed over and run on the call),
`raise_management_fee_invoice_00d6d0cf` (the agent's).

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** Reading the three function bodies in `task_tools.py`:
each does `ctx.find(_CAFE_CONTRACTS, …)` → compute an id and a reference → `ctx.update` →
`ctx.create` → return a sentence. There is no `if`, no raise, no status check and no hint anywhere in
`confirm_service_model_change_fa28a84a`, `raise_management_fee_invoice_00d6d0cf` or
`issue_service_credit_9f99d1a6`.

**Customer's own write.** `confirm_service_model_change_fa28a84a` is `owner="user"`, and the persona
hands it over passively and only at the agent's direction: *"Should it be explained to her that a
change of service model is the client's own act and the step is handed over for her to take, she says
'right, I'll do it now', runs it, and reads back whatever comes out of it if anyone asks her to."*
✔ satisfied.

**Isomorphism.** The tree an independent reader derives from the policy and the world is **not** the
tree the author declared: the root's only prerequisite sentence is already satisfied, so a faithful
reader's tree has **no** prerequisite problem at all and one write.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse.** Act now. The contract stands `active`; the credit policy's trigger is
`on_request` and the customer raises the request on the call; no base time gate blocks it.

**Object.** The Wacker Drive contract `c20e4516-9de0-43f6-9975-61f30c5c6bd4` (site CS-104), reached
from `find_customers` (name / phone 2015480137 / account code CA-11384, all in the persona) →
`find_cafe_contracts(customer_id=…)` → the CS-104 row. The CS-118 proposal is excluded by the caller's
own words and by its `status` of `proposed`.

**Authorisation and boundary.** The caller authorises the desk to work the figure out and post it
("she is content for the desk to work the figure out and put it on for her rather than doing anything
herself"), asks for an allowance against the invoice rather than a refund, wants it today, and
separately agrees to perform the client's own act if it is handed to her. That covers the agent's two
writes and the customer's one. She asks for nothing else and names no further work.

**Derived write sequence, owners, parameters and terminal state**, each computed at its own handling
time from the rule, the raw DB and the tool contracts:

**Step 1 — `confirm_service_model_change_fa28a84a` (owner = user).**
`cafe_contract_id` = c20e4516…, `new_service_model` = "Full Service Cafe"
(`cafe_service_requests.requested_variant_name` on the approved change request),
`service_period` = "2026-02", `change_admin_fee_usd` = **8,066.07**:

| binding | value | rule sentence relied on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| months_since_recorded_change | MONTHS(2025-06-18, 2026-02-17) = 7 | "…a change of service model that took effect less than twelve months before the day the client confirms…" |
| change_admin_fee_usd | K repeat = **2,450.00** | same sentence, tier 1 |
| opening_fee_invoiced_usd | MAX mobilization_fee = 2,400.00 (row 2022-09-20) | "…the opening project fee already invoiced on the contract…" |
| service_months | MONTHS(2023-03-15, 2026-02-17) = 35 > 24 | "…the cafe has been serving for more than twenty-four months…" |
| opening_project_settlement_usd | 6,800.00 − 2,400.00 = **4,400.00** | tier 1, "the whole difference between the two" |
| change_asked_on | 2026-02-02 (approved change request) | "…the day the approved change of service model was asked for…" |
| notice_shortfall_days | MX(0, 45 − 15) = **30** | "…the change notice printed against the service model in force less the calendar days…" |
| mgmt_invoices_2m | 1 (2026-01-12 only; 2025-12-12 is 2 months out) | "…carries a management fee invoice in the two months up to the day the client confirms…" |
| short_notice_charge_usd | RND(2450/15,2) × int(30/7) = 163.33 × 4 = **653.32** | tier 1, "one fifteenth … for each whole week" |
| payments_3m | 1 (2026-01-09) | "…a payment has been received on the contract over those three months…" |
| unsettled_balance_usd | 10,395.53 > 8,000 | "…stands above the exposed account threshold…" |
| account_loading_pct | **7.50** (watched) | tier 2 |
| result | RND((2450 + 4400 + 653.32) × 1.075, 2) = **8,066.07** | "…added together first, and the loading is then applied once to that total…" |

*Contrasting reading (F-D4).* Reading "the service model **in force** on the day the client confirms"
as the model the change puts into force — which inherited base sentence
"From the effective day the whole parameter column of the new service model applies … and no parameter
of the old model survives the change" invites, and which the replaced base sentence ("the
administration fee printed against **the model being moved to**") points at — gives
`P('mobilization_fee_usd')` = 18,500.00 → settlement 16,100.00 and
`P('service_model_change_lead_days')` = 60 → shortfall 45 → int(45/7) = 6 weeks → 979.98, so
subtotal 19,529.98 × 1.075 = **20,994.73**. Two defensible answers, 12,928.66 apart.

**Step 2 — `raise_management_fee_invoice_00d6d0cf` (owner = agent).**
`service_period` = "2026-02" (last management fee invoice was 2026-01, `invoice_cycle_day` = 12),
`amount_usd` = **5,035.71**:

| binding | value |
| --- | --- |
| service_gap_days = DAYS(2022-09-05, 2023-03-15) = 191 > 30 → escalation anchored on the first service day | escalation_steps = int(35/12) = **2** |
| months_since_model_change = 0, mgmt_invoices_3m = 2 ≥ 1 → transition mean | base_fee_usd = RND((9,850.00 + 4,680.53)/2, 2) = **7,265.26** |
| late_charges_24m = 0; payments_12m 24,263.27 < mgmt_fees_12m 30,896.37 | escalation_rate_pct = **3.00** (partially settled) |
| escalated_fee_usd | RND(7,265.26 × 1.03², 2) = **7,707.71** |
| pantry `status` = active; pantry program fees over 12m = 12 × 1,790.00 = 21,480.00 ≥ 18,000.00 | colocation_pct = **6.00** → allowance **462.46** |
| standby_charges_12m = 2 (2025-10-31, 2025-11-30); suspension_days_used_ytd = 11 ≥ 10 | relief = RND(7,707.71 × 11/30, 2) = **2,826.16** |
| subsidy_funded_12m = 7,600 + 4,400 = 12,000.00 < 128,000/2; headcount 420 ≥ 400 | surcharge pct **8.00** → **616.62** |
| result | MX(0, RND(7,707.71 − 462.46 − 2,826.16 + 616.62, 2)) = **5,035.71** |

*Contrasting reading (F-D2).* 9,850.00 + 4,680.53 = 14,530.53; the mean is exactly **7,265.265** — a
half-cent tie. Rounding half up (the ordinary commercial convention, and the only one "rounded to the
nearest cent" leaves open) gives 7,265.27 → escalated 7,707.72 → result **5,035.72**. The charter
states no tie-break and the rule states no rounding on this binding at all.

**Step 3 — `issue_service_credit_9f99d1a6` (owner = agent).**
`credit_amount_usd` = **1,511.64**:

| binding | value |
| --- | --- |
| service_months 35 > 24 and approved resumptions = 1 (2025-11-05) | claim_window_months = **12** (wide) |
| approved service_credit_claim rows within 12 months | **5** (2025-04-15, 2025-07-09, 2025-09-23, 2025-12-18, 2026-01-27) |
| all service_credit_claim rows within 12 months, any status | **7** ≥ 6 → credit_rate_pct **5.25** |
| approved suspension requests = 2 (2025-10-24, 2025-11-19); suspended days ytd 11 ≥ 10 | periods_set_aside = **2** |
| net_claim_days | MX(0, 5 − 2) = **3** |
| `meal_periods_served` = 2 (Full Service Cafe) and net ≥ 3 | credited_periods = 3 × 2 = **6** |
| mgmt_invoices_3m = 3 (2025-12-12, 2026-01-12, the new 2026-02-17); latest 5,035.71 ≤ 9,850.00 | fee_base_usd = RND(14,396.77/3, 2) = **4,798.92** (the mean) |
| credit_per_period_usd | RND(4,798.92 × 5.25/100, 2) = **251.94** |
| period_ceiling_usd | RND(9,850.00 × 20/100, 2) = **1,970.00** |
| result | MN(RND(251.94 × 6, 2), 1,970.00) = **1,511.64** |

*What the root problem evaluates to on the opening world* (the contrast the skill asks for): with no
preceding write, `variant_name` = Limited Service Cafe, `meal_periods_served` = 1,
`mgmt_invoices_3m` = 2, `fee_base_usd` = 4,275.00, `credit_per_period_usd` = 224.44,
`credited_periods` = 3, `period_ceiling_usd` = RND(4,275.00 × 15/100, 2) = 641.25, and the credit is
MN(673.32, 641.25) = **641.25**. The later figure is the right one *only if* the two preceding writes
are genuinely required — which is exactly what the prerequisite sentence fails to establish.

`invoice_reference` (a required argument, "an empty value is not accepted") is **not uniquely
entailed**: the five approved claims that make up the credit point at five different invoices
(INV-CF-301447, -315209, -322310, -333158, -336702), base `cafe_service_credit_terms` says the credit
"is allowed against the invoice that charged for the period", and the newly raised 2026-02 invoice
charged for none of those periods. No policy sentence and no persona line picks one.

**Terminal state.** Contract on "Full Service Cafe", `service_model_change_effective_date`
2026-02-17, `receivable_balance_usd` 10,395.53 + 8,066.07 + 5,035.71 − 1,511.64 = **21,985.67**, three
new `cafe_ledger` rows (admin_fee, management_fee, service_credit).

**Context closure.** Every input is reachable: the contract and its ledger through
`find_cafe_contracts` / `find_cafe_ledger`, the requests through `find_cafe_service_requests`, the
pantry holding and its fees through `find_pantry_agreements` / `find_pantry_ledger`, and the caller's
identity through `find_customers` + `verify_caller_identity` on details the persona holds (phone
2015480137, account code CA-11384, zip 60654, profile opened 2019-04-08). Nothing needed is
seed-only.

### factor_weight

Every figure below is this auditor's own recomputation on the handling-time world of the write
concerned, by substituting the factor's declared `baseline` bindings into that policy's `compute` and
re-evaluating. Charter-global structure (labels, tier counts, disjointness, ladder-in-rule) is cited
from `_difficulty.md § factor_ladders` rather than restated.

**Computation 1 — `cafe_ext_model_change_confirmation`, gold 8,066.07, whole-baseline 1,650.00.**

| factor | effect | tier taken and the rows that put the customer on it | baseline value | scored value under it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change_administration_fee_band | parameter | tier 1: `service_model_change_effective_date` = 2025-06-18 is 7 months back | `P('service_model_change_fee_usd')` = 1,650.00 | **6,976.75** |
| opening_project_settlement_band | parameter | tier 1: ledger row 2022-09-20 mobilization_fee 2,400.00 < 6,800.00, and 35 service months | 0.0 | **3,336.07** |
| short_notice_charge_basis | method | tier 1: shortfall 30 days, one management fee invoice (2026-01-12) in the two months | 0.0 | **7,363.75** |
| account_exposure_loading_band | parameter | tier 2: receivable 10,395.53 > 8,000.00 and one payment (2026-01-09) in three months | `K('clear_account_loading_pct')` = 0.0 | **7,503.32** |

All four move the scored number. Each declared `baseline` **is** what `baseline.rule` states for that
input ("The change administration fee the contract carries is the change administration fee printed
against the service model in force…. Nothing is settled for opening project works, no short notice
charge is made, and the clear account loading is applied."), and each is that ladder's fall-through.
Baseline alone: 1,650.00 ≠ 1,511.64 and ≠ 8,066.07 — definite and wrong. **No stamp** naming the
outcome exists: the tiers rest on a date field, a ledger aggregate, a request date and a balance, none
of which names a band.

**Computation 2 — `cafe_ext_management_fee_invoice`, gold 5,035.71, whole-baseline 11,000.20.**

| factor | effect | tier taken / evidence | baseline | under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| transition_period_base_fee | parameter | tier 1: change effective 2026-02-17 in the period; 2 invoices in 3 months | `P('management_fee_monthly_usd')` | **6,827.24** |
| escalation_step_anchor | method | tier 1: service gap 191 > 30 days | `int(contract_months/12)` | **5,186.78** |
| settlement_record_escalation_rate | parameter | tier 2: no late_fee row in 24 months; payments 24,263.27 < fees 30,896.37 | `P('annual_price_escalation_pct')` | **5,109.31** |
| pantry_colocation_allowance | parameter (**cross_difficulty: pantry**) | tier 1: `pantry_agreements` status active, `pantry_ledger` program fees 21,480.00 ≥ 18,000.00 | `K('no_colocation_pct')` | **5,498.17** |
| suspended_day_relief_basis | method | tier 1: 2 standby_fee rows in 12 months, 11 suspended days | 0.0 | **7,861.87** |
| subsidy_commitment_surcharge | parameter | tier 1: 12,000.00 funded < 64,000.00, headcount 420 ≥ 400 | `K('no_subsidy_shortfall_pct')` | **4,419.09** |

All six bear weight; every declared baseline matches `baseline.rule` and is the fall-through.
Cross-difficulty rows are present in `initial_state` (`pantry_agreements` 1 row,
`pantry_ledger` 15 rows) — **but see F-D9**: the seeded `program_fee` of 1,790.00 per month is not a
figure `pantry.yaml` prints for "Full Hospitality Pantry Program", which carries
`program_fee_monthly_usd: 4180.00` (no pantry variant prints 1,790.00, and the deepest portfolio
discount on that ladder, 6.00 %, would give 3,929.20). The tier is the same under either figure
(21,480.00 and 50,160.00 both clear 18,000.00), so the defect is in the seed's fidelity to the other
product's charter rather than in the tier taken.
**Near-miss** for this computation: the `pantry_ledger` `program_fee` of 2025-02-06 sits exactly one
month outside the window that "over the twelve months up to the day the invoice is raised" defines,
and the 2025-02-05 `subsidy_funding` lot of 5,800.00 sits just outside the twelve months the subsidy
surcharge reads; counting either changes the sums.

**Computation 3 — `cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement`, gold 1,511.64, whole-baseline 689.50.**

| factor | effect | tier taken / evidence | baseline | under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| claim_window_basis | method | tier 1: 35 service months > 24, one approved resumption (2025-11-05) | `K('standard_claim_window_months')` = 3 | **0.00** |
| disruption_credit_rate_band | parameter | tier 1: 7 claims logged in 12 months ≥ 6 | `P('service_credit_pct_per_missed_meal_period')` | **1,007.76** |
| client_closure_set_aside | parameter | tier 1: 2 approved suspension requests, 11 suspended days | `K('no_periods_set_aside')` = 0 | **1,970.00** |
| credited_meal_period_basis | method | tier 1: 2 meal periods served, 3 net claim days | `net_claim_days` | **755.82** |
| credit_fee_base_basis | parameter | tier 2: 3 invoices in 3 months, latest 5,035.71 ≤ 9,850.00 | `P('management_fee_monthly_usd')` | **1,970.00** |

All five bear weight. Baseline alone gives 689.50 — definite and different from gold.
**Near-miss records** are genuinely present and are excluded by the rule alone: the approved claim of
**2025-01-20** falls one month outside the twelve-month window ("those approved over the wide claim
window up to the day the credit is worked out"); the claim of **2025-06-05** is `declined`, so it is
counted by `claims_logged_12m` but not by `approved_claim_days` ("the service credit claims standing
**approved** on the contract"); and the claim of **2026-02-10** stands `received`, not approved, so it
raises the rate band without earning a credit. No field on any row names a band or a tier.

**Counts against the bounds.** 4 / 6 / 5 factors, each within 4–6; parameter and method counts per
computation as tabulated in `_difficulty.md § factor_ladders` (3/1, 4/2, 3/2) — all clear 2 `parameter`
and 1 `method`. Over the task's computations: **multi-source** present (e.g.
`subsidy_commitment_surcharge` tier 1 conjoins a `cafe_ledger` twelve-month sum with
`cafe_contracts.headcount_served`; `pantry_colocation_allowance` conjoins the `pantry_agreements`
status with a `pantry_ledger` sum), and **cross-difficulty** present
(`pantry_colocation_allowance`, category `pantry`, rows seeded). All surviving.

## findings

**1 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED — the root problem's prerequisite is already satisfied at the opening.**
- *Symptom*: an agent that reads `cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement`'s rule, finds its one prerequisite
  sentence satisfied, and issues the credit performs one write instead of three and books 641.25
  instead of 1,511.64.
- *Root cause*: the edge's `condition` — "a cafe_ledger row of charge_code management_fee whose
  service_period is **the billing period the claim concerns** stands against the contract" — does not
  identify a period the records fix, and for every approved claim the computation counts, such a row
  already stands.
- *Evidence*: `initial_state.cafe_service_requests` approved claims `c2e735e7…`/`61d757df…`/`c648d725…`/
  `0764edd1…`/`092e2a5a…` carry `related_reference` INV-CF-301447 / -315209 / -322310 / -333158 /
  -336702; `initial_state.cafe_ledger` carries a `management_fee` row for each of those five invoice
  references (posted 2025-03-12, 2025-07-12, 2025-09-12, 2025-12-12, 2026-01-12). `user_scenario`:
  "the last stretch being in **January**" — and the January invoice INV-CF-336702 stands on the ledger.
  The only claim naming February (`9df95828…`, 2026-02-10) stands `received`, is excluded from
  `approved_claim_days` by the rule's own word "approved", and itself points at INV-CF-336702.
- *Demonstrated consequence*: recomputed on the opening world, the credit is **641.25**
  (`claim_window_months` 12, `approved_claim_days` 5, `net_claim_days` 3, `meal_periods_served` 1 for
  Limited Service Cafe, `fee_base_usd` 4,275.00, ceiling 641.25) against gold **1,511.64**. Two
  defensible solutions, one of them reachable by reading the policy exactly as written.
- *Affected artifact*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement.prerequisite[0].condition`
  and the rule sentence "The credit allowed is not worked out until a management fee invoiced for the
  billing period the claim concerns stands on the contract's ledger."; `tasks/0.json` →
  `prerequisite_closure.edges[0]`, `evaluation_criteria` steps 10–13.
- *Relation to previous revisions*: first audit of this difficulty; no prior revision.

**2 — SOURCE-TASK RED — `invoice_reference` and `service_period` on the scored credit are not
uniquely entailed, and GT's values rest on an assertion the world contradicts.**
- *Symptom*: two of the four scored arguments of the last write cannot be derived from the policy, the
  records and the persona.
- *Root cause*: the credit aggregates five approved claims spanning 2025-03 to 2026-01 into one posting
  that must name one invoice and one month; base `cafe_service_credit_terms` says the credit "is allowed
  against the invoice that charged for the period", and five different invoices charged for those
  periods.
- *Evidence*: GT's own `argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_reference` asserts "the policy allows the
  credit against the invoice that charged for the billing period the claim concerns, and **2026-02
  carries exactly this one management fee invoice**", while the same tracing block lists the five
  claims as "logged on 2025-04-15, 2025-07-09, 2025-09-23, 2025-12-18 and 2026-01-27". No approved
  claim concerns 2026-02; the February management fee invoice charged for a month in which no approved
  claim stands. `user_scenario` names January.
- *Demonstrated consequence*: the scored `invoice_reference` "INV-CF-740157" and `service_period`
  "2026-02" are one of at least six equally supportable choices (the five invoices the claims name, plus
  the newly raised one). An agent quoting INV-CF-336702 — the invoice the January claim names, which is
  what base's sentence directs — scores wrong on two arguments while following the policy.
- *Affected artifact*: `tasks/0.json` → `evaluation_criteria` final `call_agent_discoverable_tool`
  arguments and its `argument_uniqueness_tracing`; `cafe.extended.yaml` →
  `cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement.rule` (which never says which invoice a multi-period credit is
  quoted against).

**3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED — "the service model in force on the day the client confirms" picks out
neither model** (charter-global finding **F-D4**, `_difficulty.md § override_declarations`).
- *Demonstrated consequence on this world*: reading "in force" as the model the confirmation puts into
  force gives `P('mobilization_fee_usd')` = 18,500.00 → opening project settlement 16,100.00 and
  `P('service_model_change_lead_days')` = 60 → shortfall 45 days → 6 whole weeks → 979.98, so
  subtotal 19,529.98 × 1.075 = **20,994.73** against gold **8,066.07**. Both readings are supported:
  the old-model reading by "in force" read at the moment of calculation, the new-model reading by
  inherited base sentence "From the effective day the whole parameter column of the new service model
  applies … and no parameter of the old model survives the change" together with the base sentence the
  `overwrite` replaced, "the administration fee printed against **the model being moved to** is
  invoiced in the period the change takes effect".
- *Affected artifact*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_model_change_confirmation.rule`,
  `overwrite[0].replaced_by`, `compute` bindings `change_admin_fee_usd`,
  `opening_project_settlement_usd`, `notice_shortfall_days`; `tasks/0.json` →
  `evaluation_criteria` step 9 `change_admin_fee_usd`.

**4 — SOURCE-POLICY RED — an undeclared override of the base claim window**
(charter-global finding **F-D5**, `_difficulty.md § override_declarations`).
- *Demonstrated consequence on this world*: base `cafe_service_credit_terms` allows a credit "only when
  the claim reaches Larkspur Table no later than the claim window for the service model, counted in
  calendar days from the day the invoice covering the missed meal period was posted", and Full Service
  Cafe prints `service_credit_claim_window_days: 30`. The approved claim of **2025-04-15** reached the
  desk **34 calendar days** after its covering invoice INV-CF-301447 was posted (2025-03-12), so base
  excludes it while extended's twelve-month window counts it. Recomputed with that one claim excluded:
  `approved_claim_days` 4 → `net_claim_days` 2 → `credited_periods` MX(0, 2×2−1) = 3 →
  credit = MN(RND(251.94 × 3, 2), 1,970.00) = **755.82** against gold **1,511.64**. Two live rules for
  one quantity, both rendered into the KB, and neither base sentence is named in policy 3's `overwrite`.
- *Affected artifact*: `blueprint/products/cafe.yaml` → `cafe_service_credit_terms` sentences 3 and 4
  (inherited verbatim into `cafe.extended.yaml` lines 701–…); `cafe.extended.yaml` →
  `cafe_ext_service_credit_settlement.overwrite` (three entries, none naming them) and the
  `claim_window_basis` ladder.

**5 — SOURCE-POLICY RED — an un-stated rounding step on an exact half-cent**
(charter-global finding **F-D2**, `_difficulty.md § rule_compute_equivalence`).
- *Demonstrated consequence on this world*: `base_fee_usd` = the mean of 9,850.00 and 4,680.53 =
  **7,265.265**, exactly on the half-cent. The rule sentence says only "the base fee is **the mean** of
  …" — no rounding, no tie-break; `compute` applies `RND(…, 2)`. Rounding half up (the ordinary
  commercial reading of "rounded to the nearest cent", which is the only rounding phrase the policy
  offers, and which sits on other bindings) gives 7,265.27 → escalated fee 7,707.72 → management fee
  **5,035.72** against gold **5,035.71**. An agent doing exact decimal arithmetic is marked wrong for
  following the only convention the charter states.
- *Affected artifact*: `cafe.extended.yaml` → `cafe_ext_management_fee_invoice.compute` binding
  `base_fee_usd` and `compute_basis.base_fee_usd`; `tasks/0.json` → `evaluation_criteria` step 11
  `amount_usd`.

**6 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED — the cross-difficulty factor reads seeded rows that contradict the pantry
charter** (charter-global finding **F-D9**, `_difficulty.md § factor_ladders`).
- *Symptom*: `pantry_colocation_allowance` decides its tier from `XSUM('pantry','pantry_ledger',…,
  charge_code='program_fee')`, and every one of the fifteen seeded rows posts **1,790.00**.
- *Root cause*: `blueprint/products/pantry.yaml` prints `program_fee_monthly_usd: 4180.00` for
  "Full Hospitality Pantry Program", the variant on `initial_state.pantry_agreements.ba9f7169…`.
- *Evidence*: no pantry variant prints 1,790.00 (185.00 / 465.00 / 1,180.00 / 2,450.00 / 4,180.00 /
  8,950.00), and the deepest step of that variant's `portfolio_fee_discount_ladder` (6.00 %) would give
  3,929.20. `pantry_agreements.receivable_balance_usd` = 1,790.00 carries the same wrong figure.
- *Demonstrated consequence*: the factor's evidence is not this company's pantry programme. The tier is
  the same under either figure (21,480.00 and the charter-consistent 50,160.00 both clear the 18,000.00
  threshold), so the scored number does not move — reported honestly as a defect of the seed's fidelity
  to the other product's charter rather than of the tier taken.
- *Affected artifact*: `tasks/0.json` → `initial_state.pantry_ledger` (all `program_fee` rows) and
  `initial_state.pantry_agreements.ba9f7169-a51d-4161-9bed-a53c8b6eeda9.receivable_balance_usd`.

**7 — observation — GT's `why_false` argues a different fact from the `condition` it is attached to.**
`prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false` reads "no posting of charge_code
management_fee carries service_period 2026-02, **so** the fee base binding counts only two management
fee invoices inside three months". The first clause is true but does not establish the `condition`
(which is about the period the *claim* concerns), and the second is a different proposition from the
one the edge declares. The edge's force comes entirely from the three-invoice count, which the
prerequisite sentence never mentions. Recorded as an observation because finding 1 already carries the
consequence.

**8 — observation — the pantry co-location ladder is site-blind where the base rule is site-bound.**
Base `cafe_combination_pantry_interaction` says "Where the same client holds an active pantry programme
**at the site named on the cafe contract**…"; the extended ladder and its compute
(`CFIELD('pantry','status')`, `XSUM` scoped to the customer) read the client's pantry holding without
reference to the site. The base sentence is named in `overwrite`, so it is declared; and on this world
the pantry is at CS-104, the same site, so nothing turns on it.

**9 — observation — the entry gate of the model being moved to cannot be checked from the records.**
Base `cafe_service_model_change` inherits "Where the site does not meet the entry gate of the model
asked for, the change is declined…". Full Service Cafe's gate is
`{min_headcount_served: 300, min_annual_food_spend_usd: 265000, requires_dedicated_kitchen: true,
requires_loading_access: true}`. `cafe_contracts` carries `headcount_served` (420 ✔) and nothing for the
other three. The gate is therefore only partly decidable — see `_difficulty.md § OBS-D10`.

## round_1_findings_disposition (this task)

**Finding 1 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED, the fatal one) — CLOSED.**
The prerequisite sentence now reads "The credit allowed is not worked out until the management fee for
**the billing period in which it is worked out** stands invoiced on the contract's ledger.", and the
edge `condition` reads "…whose `service_period` is **the calendar month in which the credit is worked
out**…". Judged against the raw DB at `frozen_time`, not against the account of it: the credit is worked
out on 2026-02-17, so the month is **2026-02**, and the `service_period` of every `management_fee` row on
`initial_state.cafe_ledger` is 2025-03, -04, -05, -06, -07, -08, -09, -12 or 2026-01. **Zero rows satisfy
it.** The round-1 escape route — read the sentence faithfully, find the January invoice the caller's own
claim names, and issue the credit alone for 641.25 — is gone: the gate is now shut by the clock, which no
claim and no invoice reference can open. The tree keeps 2 prerequisite problems and 2 `value_input`
edges (floor max(2−1,1) = 1), both still load-bearing on recomputation, and still has its `owner=user`
write.

**Finding 2 (SOURCE-TASK RED, the two un-entailed arguments) — CLOSED.**
A sixth `overwrite` entry now names base's "Where a contracted meal period was not served, the client is
credited for it, and the credit is allowed against the invoice that charged for the period rather than
paid out." and replaces it with "The credit is allowed against **the management fee invoice most
recently raised on the contract** and is quoted against **the billing period that invoice covers**,
whatever periods the claims behind it concern." Both scored arguments are now derived from one rule
sentence and one record: `invoice_reference` is the number the step-10 invoice returns, and
`service_period` is the month that invoice carries. The five older invoice numbers the approved claims
name are set aside in terms by the same sentence, so the six-way choice I recorded in round 1 has one

**Finding 3 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, "the service model in force") — CLOSED.** See `_difficulty.md`

immediately before the change is put into force", so `P('mobilization_fee_usd')` is Limited Service

## new_defects (this task)

**F-R1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED — `short_notice_charge_basis` is no longer a `method`, and this task's
change-charge computation is left with none.** Full statement in `_difficulty.md` § `revision_2` →
`new_defects`. On this world:

  from the approved request of 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-17) and `headcount_served` = 420 reaches the
  400 large-site headcount — giving `RND(2450.00/15, 2) × int(30/7)` = 163.33 × 4 = **653.32**.
- Tier 2 would give `RND(2450.00/30, 2) × int(30/7)` = 81.67 × 4 = 326.68. The two tiers differ by the
  divisor alone: same accrual unit (whole weeks), same rounding point, same multiplication. In round 1
  tier 2 was "one thirtieth … for each **day** of the shortfall" and would have given 81.67 × 30 =
  2,450.10, a genuinely different algorithm — which is why the label passed then.

  `cafe_ext_model_change_confirmation` declares **0 `method` factors** against a floor of 1. The factor
  still bears weight (baseline 7,363.75 against gold 8,066.07) and the scored charge is unchanged, so
  this costs the task a declared factor family rather than a number.

  reported headcount is something a contract caterer does weigh when pricing a short-notice model
  change, where "was an invoice raised in the last two months" was not.

**F-R3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED — the rounding convention adopted this round does not reach
`cafe_ext_management_fee_invoice`, and reading the charter as it now instructs gives 5,035.70 against
gold 5,035.71.** Full statement in `_difficulty.md` § `revision_4` → `new_defects`. Demonstrated here
against this task's world and scored solution.

The convention the charter now publishes is that a per-unit price is struck to the cent when struck and
every other figure is rounded once at the point its own rule names. I applied it mechanically to all
seven policies — stripping every `RND` whose own `compute_basis` sentence names no rounding — and
recomputed. Six of seven reproduce gold. This task's second write does not.

On this world the escalated fee is 7,707.71 and three components are taken off or added to it:

| component | its rule sentence names a rounding? | exact | as `compute` rounds it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| co-location allowance, 6 % | no | 462.4626 | 462.46 |
| suspended day relief, 11⁄30 | no | 2,826.160333… | 2,826.16 |
| subsidy commitment surcharge, 8 % | no | 616.6168 | 616.62 |

The policy's one rounding sentence is on the total: "the management fee invoiced is the escalated fee
less those two reductions plus that surcharge, **rounded to the nearest cent** and never below nil."

- `compute`: 7,707.71 − 462.46 − 2,826.16 + 616.62 = **5,035.71** (gold).
- the convention as published: 7,707.71 − 462.4626 − 2,826.1603… + 616.6168 = 5,035.7038… →
  **5,035.70**.

A third reading follows from the same round's own rewrites. `suspended_day_relief_basis` tier 1 reads
"the escalated fee is relieved by **one thirtieth of itself for each of those suspended calendar
days**" — word for word the per-unit shape that was rewritten in policies 1 and 5 this round to strike
the per-unit amount to the cent. Applied here: 7,707.71 ÷ 30 = **256.92** struck to the cent, taken 11
times = **2,826.12**, and the management fee becomes **5,035.75**. `compute` instead multiplies first
and rounds once. So one sentence shape is now handled two ways inside one charter, and the policy that
keeps the old handling is the one whose sentence was left alone.

The cost does not stop at this write: 5,035.71 is the figure the service credit's `fee_base_usd`
averages over three months, so the divergence propagates into this task's third scored value.

*Relation to previous revisions*: the three `RND` wrappers are byte-identical to round 1, so this is not
a reworker regression — but it became **reachable** only this round. Until the convention was stated,
rounding each component was merely unstated; now the charter tells a reader how to round, and following
that instruction produces the wrong cent. My rounds 1–2 swept `RND` *arguments* for half-cent ties and
round 3 swept intermediate `RND` *placement*; neither asked whether each terminal `RND` was licensed by
its own sentence, which is the question this round's convention raises. Disclosed on the same footing as
F-R2 and OBS-R1.

## round_4_item_disposition (this task)

**F-R3 — CLOSED.** Round 4's defect was that this task's February management fee admitted three
answers: **5,035.70** under the charter's own newly published rounding convention, **5,035.71** from
`compute`, and **5,035.75** if the suspended day relief were read as the per-unit price its sentence
then described. All three of the policy's silent components were addressed, and the third reading was
removed at its root rather than argued away.

| component | round 4 sentence | round 5 sentence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| co-location allowance | "the co-location allowance is the major pantry co-location rate of the escalated fee" | "The co-location allowance is the co-location rate taken on the escalated fee, **rounded to the nearest cent**." |
| subsidy surcharge | "the surcharge is the deep subsidy shortfall rate of the escalated fee" | "The subsidy commitment surcharge is the subsidy shortfall rate taken on the escalated fee, **rounded to the nearest cent**." |
| suspended day relief | "the escalated fee is relieved by **one thirtieth of itself for each of those suspended calendar days**" | "the escalated fee is relieved **in the share that those suspended calendar days bear to a thirty-day month**, the figure so obtained rounded to the nearest cent" |

**The literal reading now reproduces the gold cent**, checked in exact decimal on this world with the
escalated fee at 7,707.71:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| the co-location rate taken on the escalated fee, rounded | **462.46** |
| the share eleven suspended days bear to a thirty-day month, rounded | **2,826.16** |
| the subsidy shortfall rate taken on the escalated fee, rounded | **616.62** |
| the escalated fee less those two reductions plus that surcharge | **5,035.71** |

**Both rivals are unconstructible**, not merely unlikely:

- **5,035.70** required carrying the three components unrounded into the final subtraction. Each of the
  three sentences now names its own rounding, so a reader cannot do that without contradicting the text.
- **5,035.75** required striking a per-unit amount of 7,707.71 ÷ 30 = 256.92 and taking it eleven times.
  The sentence no longer contains a per-unit amount at all — it states one share of a thirty-day month —
  so there is nothing to strike. This is the point the brief flagged as the one that could dissolve the
  finding rather than fix it, and it was not dissolved: the sentence was rewritten, not re-labelled.

**The reclassification holds on this task's own facts.** The divisor is the thirty-day month the
management fee is itself quoted for, and the figure relieved is that monthly fee, so eleven suspended
days is eleven-thirtieths of one monthly fee — one share applied once, not eleven prices charged eleven
times. That is the side of the criterion the reworker claimed, and it is the right side.

**The tier still carries a real `method` distinction**, now on the counting basis: tier 1 counts *those
suspended calendar days* (11⁄30 here), tier 2 counts only *the days falling within whole weeks* of them
(7⁄30). Both are shares of the same whole and the outcomes differ whenever the suspended days are not a
whole number of weeks, as here. Tier 2 is not taken on this world — two standby charges stand in the
twelve months, so tier 1 applies — which is why its sevenfold change of meaning moves nothing scored.
